hypotheses.statement: For every integer $k\ge2$, there is a constant $c_k\in(0,1)$ with the following property. For every intersective polynomial $h\in\mathbb Z[x]$ of degree $k$ with positive leading coefficient, there are a constant $C_h\ge1$ and an integer $N_h\ge1$ such that, whenever $N\ge N_h$ and $A\subseteq[N]$ satisfy $$(A-A)\cap h(\mathbb N_+)\subseteq\{0\},$$ one has $$|A|\le C_h N^{1-c_k}.$$
There are positive integers $D_0,M$, an integer $-D_0[local:unit-condition]. Moreover, for every $n\in\mathbb N_+$, $$Mg(n)=h(r+D_0n),\qquad r+D_0n\ge1.$$

There is a threshold $P_1>\max(k,2)$, depending only on $h$, such that for every prime $p\ge P_1$ and every $l\ge1$, all but at most $k-1$ arguments modulo $p$ are regular for $F=h_l$, and at least half are regular. If Condition [local:unit-condition] holds, one may choose $P_1=P_1(k)$, uniformly over all such polynomials and chosen roots of degree $k$. For every integer $u$ with $p\nmid u$, $$\label{eq:2} \left|\mathbb E_{x\bmod p^j}e\!\left(\frac{uF(x)}{p^j}\right)\right| \le p^{-8\delta j}\quad(j\ge1), \qquad \left|\mathbb E_{\substack{x\bmod p\\x\text{ regular}}} e\!\left(\frac{uF(x)}p\right)\right| \le p^{-4\delta}.$$ The second average is normalized by the number of regular arguments.

Let $$V_k=(i^j)_{0\le i,j\le k-1},\qquad T_{k,p}=\max_{1\le j\le k}v_p(j).$$ For every prime $p[local:unit-condition], it reduces to $$S_p=T_{k,p}+v_p(\det V_k), \qquad \det V_k=\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}j!,$$ and hence depends only on $k$ and $p$.

Let $F\in\mathbb Z[x]$, let $p$ be a prime, and suppose $s=v_p(F'(x_0))<\infty$ for an integer $x_0$. If $E$ is an integer with $E\ge2s+1$, then $F$ is constant modulo $p^E$ on the argument class $x_0\bmod p^{E-s}$. For every integer $j>E$, a uniform argument in that class modulo $p^j$ gives a uniform value among the residues modulo $p^j$ congruent to $F(x_0)\bmod p^E$.
For every prime $p$ and every positive integer $l$, there are $L$ admissible residues $r_1,\ldots,r_L\bmod p^{E_p}$ such that $r_1+\cdots+r_L=0\bmod p^{E_p}$.

Let $G$ be a fixed directed graph with no loops and with at most one edge on each unordered pair of vertices. Write $e_G$ for its number of edges. All averages below use the normalized uniform measures on the indicated label configurations. Then $$\left|\mathbb E\prod_{x\to y\in E(G)}W(Y_y-Y_x)-c_p^{e_G}\right|
       \le e_Gp^{-4\delta}.$$ If every edge joins a vertex in one list $X$ to a vertex in a disjoint list $Y$, in either direction, let $K_G(X,Y)$ denote this product of edge weights. As a kernel acting by normalized averaging between the uniform $L^2$ spaces of the two lists, $$\|K_G-c_p^{e_G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \le(32e_G)^{1/4}p^{-\delta}.
 \label{eq:3}$$ Both bounds are uniform in $l$ and $p$ and include $e_G=0$, when the products are one and both errors are zero.

There is a constant $c_*>0$, independent of $l,p,S$ and the cut, such that if $b\in S$, then $$Q_S(J)\ge c_*\,
 \mathbb E_{Y,j_+} I_S(Y)
       J\bigl((Y_{u_S(v),j_v})_{v\in V_+}\bigr)^2.
 \label{eq:4}$$ Here $j_+$ consists of independent uniform indices on $V_+$.

Suppose $b\notin S$. Split the address lists into the two halves of the cut. Denote the plus lists by $Y_+$, and let $I_+(Y_+)$ be the product of the weights on edges internal to them. Put $$\mathcal D_S(J)=\mathbb E_{Y_+,j_+} I_+(Y_+)
       J\bigl((Y_{u_S(v),j_v})_{v\in V_+}\bigr)^2.$$ If $|S|\le t$, then $$Q_S(J)\ge-Cp^{-\delta}\mathcal D_S(J).
 \label{eq:5}$$ If $|S|=t+1$, then $Q_S(J)\ge0$.

If $b\notin S$ and $|S|\le t$, then, with $S'=S\cup\{b\}$, $$Q_{S'}(J)\ge c_*r_*^{-n_*}\mathcal D_S(J).
 \label{eq:6}$$

For all sufficiently large $p$, uniformly in $l$, let $\rho_p$ be either $\mu_{l,p}$ or $\mu_{l,p}^{\circ}$. For every $v\in V$ and every function $f:\mathbb F_p\to\mathbb C$ of uniform mean zero, $$\left\|\mathbb E_{\rho_p}\bigl(f(z_v)\mid
                         (z_{v'})_{v'\ne v}\bigr)\right\|_2
       \le p^{-\gamma}\|f\|_2.
 \label{eq:8}$$ The norm on the left is taken in the other-label marginal of $\rho_p$; the norm on the right is uniform on $\mathbb F_p$.

For the auxiliary family and local choices above, the threshold $P$ can be chosen as a function of $k,P_1,L,t$ alone so that Proposition 12, Lemmas 13 and 14, and [eq:9] hold uniformly in $l$. For general fixed data, $P_1$ may depend on $h$, and $L$ may depend on $h$ and its chosen roots. If $h$ satisfies Condition [local:unit-condition] and the degree-dependent choices of $P_1$, $E_p$, and $L$ from Section 2 are used, then $P$ and $M_0$ depend only on $k$.

For every positive integer $l$, finite set $\mathcal P$ of primes at least $P$, and real functions $g,g_v:X_{\mathcal P}\to\mathbb R$, $$Z_{l,\mathcal P}(g)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \left|\mathcal Z_{l,\mathcal P}((g_v)_{v\in V})\right|
 \le\prod_{v\in V} Z_{l,\mathcal P}(g_v)^{1/d}.
 \label{eq:10}$$

Fix $l\ge1$ and a finite prime set $\mathcal P$ as above. At each prime choose either $\rho_p=\mu_{l,p}$ or $\rho_p=\mu_{l,p}^{\circ}$. Let $g_v:X_{\mathcal P}\to\mathbb C$ be arbitrary functions. If, in one distinguished slot $v$, every Fourier coefficient at a denominator at most $R$ vanishes, where $R\ge1$, then $$\left|\int\prod_{u\in V}g_u(z_u)\,
                  d\bigotimes_{p\in\mathcal P}\rho_p\right|
 \le R^{-\gamma}\|g_v\|_2
                     \prod_{u\ne v}\|g_u\|_{2(d-1)}.
 \label{eq:11}$$

Let $B\subseteq\mathcal P$, fix $z_B\in X_B$, and let $G:X_{\mathcal P}\to\mathbb C$. For $1\le s<\infty$, $$\|G(z_B,\cdot)\|_{L^s(X_{\mathcal P\setminus B})} \le q_B^{1/s}\|G\|_{L^s(X_{\mathcal P})}.$$ In particular, a Fourier lift or a subfamily of its complete supports satisfies [eq:12] after specialization with the additional factor $q_B^{1/(2r)}$. The same bound holds after retaining either the remaining denominators at most a given $H\ge1$, or those greater than $H$.

For all positive integers $l,N$ and all $A\subseteq[N]$, $$Y_l(N,A)\ge\left(\frac{|A|}{N}\right)^d\ge0.$$ For every $\epsilon>0$, there is a constant $C_\epsilon$, independent of $l,N,A$, such that $$Y_l(N,A)\le C_\epsilon N^\epsilon.$$

Use the fixed parameters in [eq:14], and let $N$ be a sufficiently large integer. Suppose $1\le l\le N^\zeta$ and $$D=M_0\prod_{p\in B}p\le N^\beta,$$ where $B$ is a finite set of primes at least $P$. Let $J_1,J_2:[N]\to\mathbb C$ satisfy $|J_1|,|J_2|\le1$ and be supported in residue classes $a_1,a_2$ modulo $D$, respectively. Suppose that $r=a_2-a_1$ is admissible for $l$ modulo $D$, that $x
For the kernels just constructed, $$\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}|S_1(\alpha)-S_0(\alpha)| \ll H^{-\gamma/2}, \label{eq:18}$$ uniformly in the data of Proposition 22.

If $\alpha$ lies on the minor arcs, then, for every real $y'$ and every integer interval $I\subseteq(x_*,X]$, $$\left|\sum_{m\in I}e\bigl(\alpha F(m)+y'm\bigr)\right|
       \ll U N^{-\nu}.
 \label{eq:21}$$

For every $\alpha_0\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, write $\alpha_0=\alpha_D+\alpha_1$ for the unique decomposition in which $q(\alpha_D)$ has only prime factors dividing $D$ and $(q(\alpha_1),D)=1$. Then the coefficients defined by [eq:20] and [eq:23] satisfy $$|c(\alpha_0)-c_0(\alpha_0)|\le H^{-\gamma/2}.$$ In fact they agree when $q(\alpha_1)\le H$.
For every $l\ge1$, the proportion $\rho_l$ of good assignments under independent uniform choices of all the $s_v$ satisfies $$\rho_l\ge\rho_*:=M_0^{1-L}>0.$$

There are constants $a_0,b_0>0$ and $C_0\ge1$, depending only on the fixed polynomial $h$, its chosen roots, and the fixed structural choices, such that for all positive integers $l,N$, $$\mathcal Y_l(N)\le C_0l^{b_0}N^{-a_0}. \label{eq:33}$$ The exponents $a_0,b_0$ can be chosen as functions only of the structural parameters $k,\zeta,\sigma,M_0,\rho_*$. If the chosen roots of $h$ satisfy Condition [local:unit-condition] and the choices depending only on $k$ from Sections 2 and 3 are used, then $a_0,b_0,d$ depend only on $k$, while $C_0$ may still depend on the fixed data.

purpose: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive argument residues in each admitted class: all binary-coefficient polynomials of degree 1 through 3 with nonzero leading coefficient, primes 2 and 3, origins 0 and 1, finite derivative valuation, E=2*s+1, j=E+1, p**j<=729; separate shifted, higher-conductor and rejected boundary cases.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact closed-form uniform-lift histogram plus independent SymPy polynomial evaluation of every argument in the class; no solver witnesses.

title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
